text: Confirmed the read-modify-write culprit — now shipping an atomic fix.

checks.name: same_behaviour
checks.detail: 40 sequential requests matched the original exactly

args.fix: Replaced read-modify-write (SELECT then UPDATE with client-computed value) with single atomic UPDATE statements: deposit uses UPDATE ... SET balance = balance + %s; withdraw uses conditional UPDATE ... SET balance = balance - %s WHERE balance >= %s and distinguishes unknown-account vs InsufficientFunds with a follow-up SELECT only on failure. The atomic UPDATE holds the row lock while computing, so concurrent increments/decrements serialize correctly without extra locking.
args.root_cause: Lost update from SELECT-then-UPDATE race: deposit/withdraw both read balance then write balance +/- amount computed from the stale read. Two concurrent txns read the same old balance (e.g., both read 100), then each writes old +/- amount, so one overwrites the other (both write 200 instead of 300). The second UPDATE blocks on the first's row lock but still uses its stale read, so committed balances fall short of the sum of successful ops.

text: Fix accepted. Root cause was a lost-update race (`SELECT balance` then `UPDATE balance = stale ± amount`); fixed with single atomic `UPDATE ... SET balance = balance ± %s` (conditional on `balance >= %s` for withdraw).
